minutes.headline: Select Board approved all 2021 license renewals, ratified four police appointments, and began FY22 budget priorities.
minutes.summary: The board waived the town's right of first refusal on a Chapter 61A parcel, reviewed a draft host community agreement with a cannabis retailer, and ratified four police appointments. It approved annual license renewals, with alcohol renewals contingent on safety inspections and state tax good-standing certificates, on a split vote. It discussed FY22 budget priorities and the appointment process for boards, which ended without agreement, with members asked to submit their own proposals.

public_comment.topic: Trash bags are repeatedly out of stock at stores; asks the town manager and DPW director to add an option to order bags online.

decisions.decision: Board will collect all questions on the draft cannabis host agreement, wait a couple of days for the applicant's input, then send them to town counsel; the community outreach meeting is aimed for mid-January with 14 days' newspaper notice.
Town manager to ask counsel to clarify section 2.8 on cost reimbursement, the first-year-only revenue wording, and the assignment clause.
Lonnie's Orchard added to the alcohol renewal list after the town manager confirmed it had paid.
Each board member will submit a proposed appointment process to the town manager, who will distribute them to all five at once; the topic returns at a later workshop.
Town manager to ask town counsel whether the Conservation Commission has authority to ban possession of firearms on land it controls.

what_happened.line: The Select Board approved 2021 alcohol license renewals 3-2, contingent on safety inspections and state tax good-standing certificates.
The board approved the auto dealer, limousine, common victualler, miscellaneous and weekday entertainment license renewals.
The board ratified or made four police appointments: a lieutenant, a sergeant and two full-time officers.
The board reviewed a draft cannabis host community agreement, took no vote, and will send its questions to town counsel.
The board waived the town's right of first refusal on a Chapter 61A parcel at 360 Flat Hill Road.

why_it_matters: The cannabis host agreement sets what the company pays the town and what costs it reimburses, so the wording counsel returns affects town revenue in every year of the agreement.

The town manager's FY22 notes point to a pay-as-you-throw trash contract expected to rise when bid and to free cash held as a cushion against lower state aid, both of which bear on residents' bills and the town budget, mostly taxes.
watch_next: Town counsel's answers on the draft host agreement, and the community outreach meeting aimed for mid-January with 14 days' newspaper notice.
Each board member's proposed appointment process, to be circulated by the town manager and taken up at a later workshop.
